clauses.title: Scope – Requirements regarding material, sizes,
clauses.text: 1. Scope - Requirements regarding material, sizes, construction, workmanship and finish of ledged, braced and battened timber door shutters.

clauses.title: Timber – Suitable for
clauses.text: 2.1 Timber -  Suitable for manufacture shall be as per IS 12896 : 1990.*  Moisture content shall be between 8 to 14 percent.

clauses.title: All timbers shall be kiln
clauses.text: 2.2 All timbers shall be kiln  seasoned. Sapwood of durable species and heartwood and sapwood of nondurable species shall be treated with suitable preservative (except the water soluble leachable type).

clauses.title: Timber shall be free
clauses.text: 2.3 Timber shall be free from decay, fungal growth, boxed heart, pitch pockets or streakes on the exposed edges, borer holes, splits and cracks.

clauses.title: Timber shall be graded
clauses.text: 2.4 Timber shall be graded as first or second grade as given in Table 1 of the standard on the basis of permissible defects.

clauses.title: Designation – Door shutter
clauses.text: 3. Designation -  Door shutter shall be designated by symbols denoting the width, type and height of door in succession in the following manner : a) Width -It shall be indicated by the number of modules of 100 mm in the width of door opening. b) Type - D = Door, S = Single shutter, T = Double leaf shutter. c) Height - It shall be indicated by the number of modules of 100 mm in the height of door opening. TABLE 1 DIMENSION OF DOOR SHUTTERS Designation ` Width Height of  Doors mm mm 8 DS 20 700 1905 (1945) 8 DS 21 700 2005 (2045) 9 DS 20 800 1905 (1945) 9 DS 21 800 2005 (2045) 10 DS 20 900 1905 (1945) 10 DS 21 900 2005 (2045) 12 DT 20 1100+ 1905 (1945) 12 DT 21 1100+ 2005 (2045) *  Classification of indian timbers for doors and window shutters and frames. +   Combined width of double leaf shutter in closed position. Note - In arriving at the standard widths and heights,and allowance has been made of 60 mm for door   frames, 40 mm forfloor finish and 5 mm clearance all round  and 15 mm for rebate all round for the shutter into the frame. Example -  8 DS 21 would mean a shutter suitable for a single shutter door of 8 module width and 21 module height.

clauses.title: Dimension and Tolerances
clauses.text: 4. Dimension and Tolerances Description Width Thickness mm mm Top and bottom edges 150 ±1.5 25 ±1.5 Middle Ledge 200 ±1.5 25 ±1.5 Braces 110 to 125 25 ±1.5 Battens 140 to 160 25 ±1.5 (depending upon the width of the shutter) Tolerances of sizes of door shutter shall be ± 3mm.

clauses.title: Workmanship and Finish –
clauses.text: 5. Workmanship and Finish - All battens of the shutter shall be sanded and finished smooth.

clauses.title: Defective knots, where permitted in surfaces
clauses.text: 5.1 Defective knots, where permitted in surfaces exposed to view, shall be completely bored or cut out and tightly plugged with cross-gained plug (round or dovetailed) of similar spices of timber and shall be properly glued. All the surfaces of door shutters which are required to be painted or polished or varnished ultimately shall be covered initially before delivery by protective coat of primer polish or varnish.

clauses.title: Tests
clauses.text: 6. Tests a) Slamming test, b) Shock resistance test, c) Edge loading test and d) Resistance to buckling test type tests only. For detailed information, refer  to  IS 6198 : 1992. Specification for ledged, braced and battened timber door shutters (second revision).
